correctness.rationale: For d=n−2, the recurrence coordinates a^(d−s)P_s give a unitriangular integral change from the degree-d monomial basis, hence the Veronese curve over any field. On the characteristic-zero distinct-root chart the reciprocal roots turn each Toeplitz entry into a common scalar times μ^iλ^j−λ^iμ^j, so all substituted Pfaffians are zero as integral polynomials and stay zero modulo every characteristic. For a putative relation among the selected quadrics, extract the maximum weight i+j of a participating term. At that weight the leading differences form a chain, and the outer monomial of the smallest participating first index survives. This proves independence including in characteristic two. The number of quadrics equals dim J_2=binom(d+2,2)−(2d+1)=binom(d,2), and J is generated by its catalecticant quadrics, so equality is of ideals, not just of radicals or point sets. The Veronese Hilbert function dm+1 and the minimal Eagon–Northcott resolution of the 2-by-d minors (height d−1) give exactly the claimed series and Betti numbers. Smoothness and integrality persist after base change.
residual_risks: Bounded replay does not cover all sizes or fields; the uniform proof does. No claim of formal verification or specialist attestation.

value.rationale: The natural equal-diagonal section is sufficiently special that ambient rank-locus theory does not decide whether it has extra components or thickening. Identifying it uniformly with the Veronese ideal, even in characteristic two, and extracting a minimal basis from explicit principal Pfaffians gives a usable structural description rather than an instance computation. The standard numerical invariants are useful consequences, not the primary contribution.
residual_risks: No higher-rank or general structured linear-section claim.
